message.content:
I need to find where memo-related derived metadata is computed from memo content in this repository. This metadata is used for lists/previews and is computed automatically rather than set by the user. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Any function or method that computes/extracts metadata from memo content (e.g. title, snippet, preview, summary, etc.)
2. Look for terms like "memo" combined with "metadata", "snippet", "preview", "title", "extract", "derive", "compute", "parse"
3. Check store files, service files, or utility files related to memos
4. Look for patterns where memo content is parsed to extract properties like title, description, snippet, etc.

Search breadth: very thorough

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

65	func (s *APIV1Service) RegisterGateway(ctx context.Context, echoServer *echo.Echo) error {
66		// Shared authorizer: one source of truth for authentication and anonymous-access
67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {
80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {
81						http.Error(w, `{"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}`, http.StatusUnauthorized)
82						return
83					}
84				}
85	
86				// Apply the identity to the context (no-op for permitted anonymous requests).
87				if result != nil {
88					r = r.WithContext(auth.ApplyToContext(ctx, result))
89				}
90	
91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}
94	
95		// Create gRPC-Gateway mux with auth middleware.
96		gwMux := runtime.NewServeMux(
97			runtime.WithMiddlewares(gatewayAuthMiddleware),
98		)
99		if err := v1pb.RegisterInstanceServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if err := v1pb.RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {

109			return err

113		}

118			return err
119		}

content.text:
Here is a comprehensive summary of all memo-related derived metadata computation in this repository.

---

## Memo-Derived Metadata: Complete Analysis

There are two major categories of derived metadata computed from memo content: **stored properties** (persisted in the database payload) and **on-the-fly computed values** (generated at response time). Both are server-side computations driven by the markdown parsing service.

---

### 1. Core Markdown Service -- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`

This is the central engine for all metadata extraction. It defines a `Service` interface with these key methods:

- **`ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)`** (line 33) -- The most efficient entry point. Parses markdown once and extracts all metadata in a single AST walk. Returns an `ExtractedData` struct (line 21) containing:
  - `Tags []string` -- all `#tag` nodes found in the content
  - `Mentions []string` -- all `@mention` nodes (lowercased)
  - `Property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property` -- the computed boolean/string properties (see below)

- **`ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)`** (line 192) -- Extracts just the boolean/string properties by walking the AST. The property struct fields are:
  - `HasLink` (bool) -- whether content contains any markdown link
  - `HasTaskList` (bool) -- whether content contains GFM task checkboxes
  - `HasCode` (bool) -- whether content contains code blocks or inline code spans
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` (bool) -- whether any task checkbox is unchecked
  - `Title` (string) -- extracted from the **first block-level child** of the document **if and only if** it is an H1 heading (`# ...`). The plain text is extracted recursively from the heading's child nodes (stripping inline formatting like bold/italic). See `extractHeadingText()` at line 173.

- **`ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)`** (line 143) -- Extracts just the `#tag` nodes, deduplicating them while preserving case.

- **`GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)`** (line 264) -- Generates a plain-text summary/snippet from the markdown content. It walks the AST and:
  - Extracts text from `Text` nodes, auto-links, and tag nodes
  - Skips code blocks (fenced and indented) entirely
  - Inserts spaces between block-level elements (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells/rows)
  - Preserves inline code text, image alt text, strikethrough text
  - Truncates at a word boundary using `truncateAtWord()` (line 472) if the result exceeds `maxLength`

---

### 2. Protobuf Definitions for Stored Properties

**`/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`** (the storage-layer schema, line 7):
```protobuf
message MemoPayload {
  Property property = 1;
  Location location = 2;
  repeated string tags = 3;

  message Property {
    bool has_link = 1;
    bool has_task_list = 2;
    bool has_code = 3;
    bool has_incomplete_tasks = 4;
    string title = 5;  // from first H1 heading
  }
}
```

**`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`** (the API-layer schema, lines 255-279):
- `Property property = 15` -- OUTPUT_ONLY computed properties (same fields as storage)
- `string snippet = 17` -- OUTPUT_ONLY plain-text snippet (not stored, computed on the fly)
- `repeated string tags = 10` -- OUTPUT_ONLY extracted tags

---

### 3. Payload Rebuilder -- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`

The function **`RebuildMemoPayload()`** (line 74) is the single entry point that computes and persists derived metadata into `memo.Payload`:

```go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
    // ...
    data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
    // ...
    memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
    memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
    return nil
}
```

This function is called in three places:

1. **On memo creation** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108:
   ```go
   if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil { ... }
   ```

2. **On memo content update** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 447:
   ```go
   if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil { ... }
   ```

3. **Batch rebuild of all memos** -- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` line 27 (`RunOnce` method), which iterates over all memos in batches of 100 and rebuilds each one.

---

### 4. Snippet Generation (computed on the fly, not stored)

The snippet is NOT stored in the database. It is computed at response time via:

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`** line 83:
```go
func (s *APIV1Service) getMemoContentSnippet(content string) (string, error) {
    snippet, err := s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)
    // ...
}
```

This is called from:

- **`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators()`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` line 76 -- sets `memoMessage.Snippet` on every memo returned via the API.
- **`batchConvertMemoRelations()`** in the same file, lines 225 and 248 -- generates snippets for related memos shown in relation metadata.
- **`convertMemoRelationFromStore()`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` lines 154 and 162 -- snippets for individual memo relation lookups.
- **`memoNotificationSnippet()`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` line 318 -- snippets for comment and mention notification payloads.

---

### 5. Property Conversion for API Responses

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`** line 315:
```go
func convertMemoPropertyFromStore(property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property) *v1pb.Memo_Property {
    return &v1pb.Memo_Property{
        HasLink:            property.HasLink,
        HasTaskList:        property.HasTaskList,
        HasCode:            property.HasCode,
        HasIncompleteTasks: property.HasIncompleteTasks,
        Title:              property.Title,
    }
}
```

This is called at line 49 when converting a stored memo to an API response, mapping `memo.Payload.Property` to the output `memoMessage.Property`.

---

### 6. Mention Extraction for Notifications

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`** line 26:
The `resolveMentionTargets()` method calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll()` to extract `@mention` usernames from memo content. These are used to dispatch inbox notifications when a memo mentions another user.

---

### 7. Markdown Service Initialization

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`** line 48:
```go
markdownService := markdown.NewService(
    markdown.WithTagExtension(),
    markdown.WithMentionExtension(),
)
```

The service is created with both the tag and mention goldmark extensions enabled.

---

### Summary of All Derived Metadata Fields

| Field | Stored? | Computed Where | Description |
|-------|---------|---------------|-------------|
| `tags` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` | All `#tag` tokens found in content |
| `property.title` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | Plain text of first H1 heading (if first block element) |
| `property.has_link` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | Content contains markdown links |
| `property.has_task_list` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | Content contains GFM task checkboxes |
| `property.has_code` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | Content contains code blocks or inline code |
| `property.has_incomplete_tasks` | Yes (payload) | `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` | Content has unchecked task checkboxes |
| `snippet` | No (on-the-fly) | `GenerateSnippet` | Plain-text summary, max 64 chars, truncated at word boundary |
| `mentions` | No (transient) | `ExtractAll` | `@username` references, used for notification dispatch |
